greeting.text: Oh. Sam. Hi. It's Judy. From the office. Yes, I work here now. Don't make the face.

options.sam: Hi Judy. Good to see you. I'd like to purchase a ticket.

judy.text: Good to see you too. A ticket. Yes. That's what I do now. I sell the tickets. It's a transition period, Sam, people have those.

options.sam: Judy! From the office! Wow. One ticket, please.

judy.text: Don't 'wow' me. I know how it looks. I ran a department, and now I'm in a glass box with a lanyard. It's very temporary. One ticket. Fine.

options.sam: I finished the spreadsheet, actually. Can I get a ticket?

judy.text: You did not finish the spreadsheet. I checked after you left. And please don't tell anyone from the office you saw me here. A ticket.

core.text: So the way it works now, and I'm only explaining this because you're staring, is I've got the little machine. You tap it, it prints, I tear along the dotted line, except the dotted line is more of a suggestion since they changed paper vendors. The old vendor was a family business, lovely people, the daughter went to dental school. The new vendor is just a website. You can't call a website, Sam. I tried. I was on hold with a website for forty minutes, and my manager, who is nineteen, came over and asked if I needed help. With a phone. I managed a budget of four million dollars. Anyway. That's the machine. It's over here. I'll get to it.

judy.text: I'm getting to it. Patience, Sam. I've got all day. That's the thing about this job. I've got all day.

options.sam: I'm so sorry about the website. Could I get a ticket?

judy.text: Thank you, that's kind. Don't be kind, Sam, it makes it worse. I can take rude. I had surgeons yelling at me for twenty-six years.

options.sam: The manager who is nineteen, yes. Is the ticket in the machine?

judy.text: The ticket is in the machine, yes. He calls me young lady. I was Chief Operating Officer of a company that makes hips, Sam. He doesn't know what a hip costs.

core.text: So here's what happened, since you're going to ask. I retired. Twenty-six years as Chief Operating Officer. Every hip, every knee, every little titanium screw that went into a person had a piece of paper under it, and the paper came across my desk. You brought me the paper. Then there was a cake with my name spelled wrong, and then it's Tuesday, and then it's every Tuesday. So I went to China. By myself. Spent the retirement on it, more or less. I'm not apologizing for China. The Wall is long, Sam. And I came back, and the house was very quiet, and this place had a sign in the window. There's a form I had to sign to work here. No indemnification clause. I offered to fix it. They said no.

options.sam: That sounds amazing. One ticket, when you get a chance.

judy.text: It was amazing. You should go. Not now, you have a movie. And you never used your vacation days, I had to sign off on all of that. I had sign-off, Sam. I had a stamp.

options.sam: I'm sorry about the cake. Ticket?

judy.text: J, U, D, I. With an I. Twenty-six years and a seat on the executive committee. They spelled it right on my name tag, I'll give them that. It's the one thing in here that's right.

options.sam: No indemnification clause? Does it at least have my ticket?

judy.text: The form doesn't have your ticket, the machine has your ticket. The form just has me. Unprotected, in a glass box. Twenty-six years of telling surgeons not to sign things, and I signed it. Don't tell the surgeons.

core.text: Anyway. The thing about the Wall is you can't see the end of it from where you're standing. You just have to go. I'm just telling you that. This booth isn't the end of the wall either. I've got time, Sam. That's the one thing this job gives you.

final.text: All right. Here's a ticket. Second row, on the aisle, it has your name on it. It's good to see you, Sam. Really. Don't tell anyone.

pa.text: Sam, if you can hear this, the popcorn is not complimentary. Management made me say that. Enjoy the film.
